concepts.title: Map Scale, Representative Fraction and Ground Distance
concepts.definition: Map scale expresses the ratio between map distance and ground distance as a statement, a representative fraction such as 1:50,000 or a linear graphical scale, and the actual ground distance equals the map distance multiplied by the scale value.
concepts.key_idea: The representative fraction is unit free, so one inch on a 1:63,360 map means one mile on the ground.

concepts.title: Conversion of Scales and Construction of Graphical Scale
concepts.definition: Converting scales changes a statement or fraction from metric to English units or vice versa using the relation that one inch equals 2.54 cm, and a graphical linear scale is constructed with primary and secondary divisions so that distance can be read directly even after map enlargement or reduction.
concepts.key_idea: A graphical scale keeps its truth when the map is photographically enlarged or reduced, which is its great advantage over verbal and fractional scales.

concepts.title: Uses of Scales and Their Choice for Different Maps
concepts.definition: The choice of scale depends on the purpose and extent of the map: large scales of 1:25,000 show cadastral detail, 1:50,000 topographical sheets serve field studies, and small scales of 1:1 million or more serve atlases and wall maps, since finer detail needs larger scale.
concepts.key_idea: Scale controls generalisation: small scale maps must omit and simplify features, while large scale maps preserve positional accuracy.
